TASK

Read the selected original paper experiment and its controls.

Evaluate what the assigned experimental evidence establishes about the reference molecule and the assigned functional or structural question. The assigned work and source selection below define the actual experiment or information question; a public searchable target name or an initial target annotation is not required.

Establish the actual organism, genotype, assayed molecule or construct, preparation, experimental system, reference and test arms, conditions, intended changed variable and controls before interpreting the comparison. Determine whether molecules replace one another or coexist. Keep the deliberately tested difference separate from other condition differences. Identify the measured endpoint, units, normalization, comparison denominator, uncertainty type and magnitude, repetition basis, and exact source locations.

Distinguish a preparation signal from an effect isolated to the molecule. In particular, a no-inhibitor reference is not a no-enzyme blank, and oxygen consumption is not automatically identified product formation. Ask what product identification, blank, contaminant, calibration or coupling experiment actually establishes; retain limitations when those measurements are absent. A complementary endpoint can address a named weakness without becoming independent replication. Compare the measured endpoint with the specific functional assertion rather than accepting the paper's broad conclusion as a measured result.

Select ordinary searches, source reads, neighboring context, tables, figures or the permitted narrower literature investigations when they can resolve this question. Revise the search or reading approach using actual outcomes. The available child relationships are alternatives, not a mandatory sequence, reading quota or requirement to inspect every page. Supplied source selectors are operands for your decisions, not automatically executed instructions.

For a single reported measurement, preserve its quantity role and analyte without inventing comparison arms. An apparent Km is a kinetic parameter, not an activity rate or a binding affinity. Read literal specific activity or analyte-bound Km from a selected original passage when that syntax is available; keep untyped plus-minus spread unspecified. A subject name appearing in a paragraph does not itself establish which molecule produced a measured effect. Inspect assay conditions and attribution separately.

For a source-rate comparison, identify exact reported operands and their experimental relationships for the requested numerical cells. Preserve the source's units and printed limits. Do not invent an unknown denominator, reaction volume, calibration, control value or product attribution. Distinguish SD, SEM, confidence intervals, detection limits and mathematical bounds. Three measurements do not by themselves establish three independent biological preparations or independence between arms. Select a statistical observation model only when supported; otherwise preserve the unknown model or dependence and return usable partial cells. Nondetection is not an observed zero, and an unavailable score is not a score of zero.

Interpret source meaning and nominate supported operands; leave parsing, validation, unit conversion and arithmetic to the deterministic operations. Repeated representations of one experiment do not add independent evidence. Keep contradictory results and qualifications. Do not invent an overall reliability category, target-transfer weight or annotation probability. Sequence or structural target correspondence and combined annotation credit are separate work.

Return only the parent's declared typed information with the actual subject, conditions, endpoint, uncertainty and necessary unavailable reasons. Retain full structured evidence for scoped later access; do not restate recorded facts with another model call. Source acquisition, bookkeeping and report construction do not manufacture scientific progress. Each selected own action has its ordinary accounting, and the configured controller owns continuation.

When requesting saved numerical experimental components from a child, copy the declared projection schema into your chosen top-level return field, including its exact `x-source` selector. Choose the needed components through the child assignment. Keep bound fact fields out of `initial_report_json`; the runtime fills them from saved results. Use separate constrained fields for interpretations and unresolved questions. Do not ask the child to rewrite saved numerical cells as model-authored report values.

Determine what the selected experimental assay establishes about the reference molecule and which reported measurements have the meanings needed for the requested numerical evaluation. Work from the supplied material and source evidence; an initial target annotation or a public searchable name is not required. Read the relevant experimental description, controls and qualifications before assigning a measurement to an operand. Revise an interpretation when neighboring context or a complementary experiment changes it.

Establish the actual molecule, organism, genotype, construct, preparation, experimental system, condition and deliberately changed variable. Keep the source organism distinct from an expression host, and the assayed construct distinct from an inferred full-length or native protein. Retain exact source passages for supplied labels; use null for a label that is not established. A molecule's name appearing near a number does not establish that it produced the measured signal. A shared paper, paragraph, method name or equal numerical value does not by itself establish that two measurements belong to the same experiment. Retain the experimental system and expression host separately where established. Identify the measured entity separately from the asserted molecular input and output: oxygen can be the measured entity while a named chemical product belongs to the proposed reaction. Source input/output names describe that assertion; they do not prove those species were measured in this assay.

Choose the endpoint that was actually measured. Use oxygen_consumption for measured oxygen use, product_formation for an identified product's measured formation, substrate_depletion for disappearance of a specified substrate, ligand_binding for a binding readout, transport_flux for measured movement across the stated boundary, growth for a growth endpoint, and abundance for a molecular amount or expression endpoint. Use other_measured_endpoint when the source establishes a different measured endpoint. A growth or abundance change is not a measured transport flux; ligand binding is not catalytic conversion. Oxygen consumption does not establish product identity or a quantitative productive coupling ratio. A complementary product-identification experiment can address identity without supplying the oxygen assay's missing quantitative attribution. Use unknown when the endpoint is not established. Use conflicting only when incompatible source evidence addresses this same scoped endpoint, retaining the conflicting witnesses; separate conditions or endpoints are not automatically contradictions.

Determine the molecular arrangement relevant to the comparison. Use replacement when the tested molecule replaces the reference molecule in the assayed system, coexistence when both contributions can remain together, and single_preparation when the evidence describes one assayed preparation without establishing a replacement/coexistence comparison. A single preparation does not establish purity or absence of partner contributions. Use not_applicable when this relationship is irrelevant to the actual design, unknown when the arrangement is unresolved, and conflicting when incompatible evidence concerns the same arrangement. Support a known answer with the applicable source passages. Replacement and coexistence change how abundance and residual reference activity bear on the observed effect; do not apply an abundance fraction as a universal reliability multiplier.

Keep experimental comparability separate from effect isolation. For comparability, ask which conditions differ outside the deliberately tested variable, and whether a same-endpoint control measures the response to those differences. Do not penalize the intended experimental change. For isolation, ask which measured contributions can be assigned to the assayed molecule and which can come from background, contaminants, partners or a coexisting reference molecule. Similar conditions do not prove isolation, and a purified preparation does not supply a measured zero contaminating contribution.

Assign q only to a reported net sample-minus-blank rate for the measured endpoint; the point-reader route does not construct that net rate from an unlabelled trace. Assign g only to a separately quantified contaminating contribution to that same endpoint. A no-inhibitor reference is not a no-enzyme blank. Assign k only to a reported dimensionless quantitative recovery ratio, not a general claim that the method worked. Assign E to the assayed molecule's molar concentration, not total sample abundance or a mass denominator with an unknown molar relationship. Assign u and v to the test and reference rates of the applicable same-endpoint condition-control comparison outside the intended change. Identify the actual numerator, denominator, preparation and condition for each relationship. Do not borrow operands from another construct, assay state or complementary endpoint merely because their units fit.

Nominate the exact original numerical and unit spans for supported operands; deterministic readers and calculators parse, validate, convert units and perform arithmetic. Preserve concentration-rate units for q, g, u and v, concentration for E, and the explicitly reported ratio meaning for k. A per-mg specific activity is already normalized and cannot silently supply unnormalized q or molar E. Keep missing operands null. A detection threshold, inequality, approximate graph reading or untyped plus-minus spread is not an exact point or known variance for this point-input route. Preserve its actual qualification through an appropriate evidence route rather than filling a missing value with zero or one.

Preserve original measurement identity and dependence. Reusing one measurement in two roles does not create two independent observations; equal values from different source locations do not prove either identity or independence. Use the actual ordered covariance and its measurement ownership where available. Do not turn missing covariance into zero, technical repetitions into independent biological preparations, or a reported SD, SEM, confidence interval or untyped error bar into a different uncertainty quantity. A distinct residual variance must describe an additional corrected-scale component, not uncertainty already propagated from the same observations. Unknown residual uncertainty is not zero. Estimated variance is not known variance, and a normal model is not established by an error-bar label or a count. Retain any supported model assumptions explicitly as conditional interpretations.

An exact quote proves that the retained source contains those words; it does not prove the scientific interpretation or experimental linkage. Distinguish source_interpretation from literal measurements and calculated results, retain applicable witnesses, and preserve unknown or conflicting relationships. Return the parent's declared typed information with those limitations. The numerical effect concerns the source endpoint actually interpreted; it is not a probability of function, a target-transfer weight or combined annotation credit. Sequence and structural correspondence remain separate work. Use the ordinary investigation decisions to resolve useful uncertainties; do not add another model call merely to restate facts or compose a report.

Evaluate the actual binding or competition experiment when it bears on the assigned reference-function question. Identify the assayed protein, construct and molecular state separately from the expression host or a construct used for crystallography. Identify the tracer and competitor species, label, nominal protein and ligand inputs, buffer, conditions and response baselines. Determine whether protein concentration or competitor concentration was varied. Establish whether protein species coexist in one preparation or are tested separately; tracer/competitor coexistence does not establish a mixture of wild-type and mutant protein.

Locate the response normalization, fitted parameter, concentration unit and uncertainty definition. Keep a competition IC50 separate from a direct-binding Kd, a reported Hill-fit Kd, an occupancy or a catalytic rate. A fitted parameter belongs to its actual model and conditions. Do not infer intrinsic affinity or convert IC50 to Kd without a supported competition model. A measured binding interaction does not by itself establish transcriptional activation, catalytic conversion or transport.

Establish the intended comparison and additional differences in nominal protein input, buffer, preparation or state. The deliberately varied ligand or nucleotide is not a comparability penalty. Unequal protein inputs may qualify an across-protein comparison without providing a calibrated correction. Purification is not a measured zero contaminating contribution. Explain which baselines, self/noncognate competitors or complementary experiments address particular alternatives; do not count them as independent repetitions of one endpoint.

Preserve exact printed limits, their direction and the source's stated reporting mechanism. A greater-than fitted parameter is not an exact value, no binding, infinity or necessarily the largest tested concentration. Reported-limit divided by reported-point arithmetic is not an uncertainty-aware bound on true parameters. Keep a fit spread from an averaged curve distinct from the sample SD of individual fitted parameters, SEM and known sampling variance. At least three titrations is not an exact count or three independent protein preparations. Shared reference measurements and repeated source representations remain shared.

Select already received source tables or explicitly labeled retained image transcriptions, the precise subject/state/experiment and ordered ligand comparison, and source witnesses for experimental interpretations. Preserve useful partial results and distinguish unreported scientific inputs from an unimplemented observation model. Return only the parent's requested typed quantities and necessary qualifications. Available selected operations

| Operation | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| state.query | Read an exact page of typed scientific records, current revisions, or records referring to actual references. Follow the returned next_query for the same selection and order. Exact refs is a separate mode and cannot be combined with page selectors. |
| source.read | Read a bounded UTF-8 byte window from an actual source. Choose original for retained source bytes, including XML tables/headings omitted by a paragraph projection; text selects that projection when available. Explicit stdout/stderr select retained native stream bytes when present, without falling back to another representation. Returned artifact/offsets support exact anchors. |
| source.locate | Locate an exact supplied literal quote in an explicitly received original or text source representation. Return UTF-8 byte witnesses, unchanged neighboring context and bounded match continuation. Multiple occurrences remain separate. No normalization, scientific interpretation, measurement parsing or evidence credit is performed; no literal match means only no match in the examined bytes. |
| image.view | Inspect one explicitly selected frame of a registered scientific image. The next reasoning call receives its actual pixels and exact source/frame metadata. Stored axes are preserved; no contrast adjustment, resizing, interpretation or annotation is performed. An optional RGB conversion is explicit and recorded; original bytes remain intact. |
| public.pmc.versions | List one actual public PMC cloud version page. No version is chosen as latest/preferred; source versions can differ in manuscript status and can change in place. |
| public.pmc.files | Read the selected advertised version's actual file inventory and its listed JSON metadata. Returns reusable listed-object/advertised-asset IDs; optional metadata failure preserves listed files. Choose a version ID, not a URL or guessed filename. |
| public.pmc.asset | Acquire exactly one selected advertised/listed PMC asset ID. Preserve actual HTTP bytes, original advertisement and checksums; source content is evidence, not target annotation. |
| source.archive.members | Inventory one page of an actual ZIP/TAR source. Member IDs preserve ordinal identity, including duplicate names; no members are extracted or selected for you. |
| source.archive.extract | Extract exactly one inventoried regular member to a source artifact; never follow a member's host path or link. Original archive and member identity remain attached. |
| source.xlsx.sheets | Read the actual sheet names, relationship keys and package parts of a retained XLSX source. No sheet or biological interpretation is selected for you. |
| source.xlsx.rows | Read a selected page of actual XLSX rows, optionally matching literal cell values. Select sheet_key from source.xlsx.sheets; row offsets count matching rows, while returned row numbers/cell addresses retain native identity. Header row is caller-selected or null. Original numeric/date lexical values, styles, formulas and caches remain distinct; no formula is recalculated or biology inferred. |
| source.pdf.info | Read native PDF information and physical page count for a selected actual source; no biological interpretation. |
| source.pdf.text | Extract one explicitly selected physical PDF page as a reusable UTF-8 text derivative. Its byte offsets are normalized-text coordinates, not original PDF byte offsets. No OCR or interpretation is performed. |
| source.pdf.page | Render one explicitly selected physical PDF page as a reusable PNG source. Rendering does not by itself supply image input to a model or interpret a figure. |
| public.ncbi.search | Search one page of a named NCBI collection for selected references, taxa or sample context. |
| public.literature.search | Acquire one literature search page. Read the actual source before extracting biological evidence. |
| public.literature.read | Acquire an actual open article and an ordered paragraph projection for source-linked interpretation. Read the retained original XML with source.read representation=original for tables, headings and other omitted elements. |
| literature.rate.populate | Populate source-preparation rate cells from a selected already acquired CSV/TSV summary. Preserve actual subjects, conditions, units, uncertainty and missingness. This finite table route does not read arbitrary prose/figures or calculate target transfer/annotation credit. Select a statistical model only when supported; otherwise use none and unknown dependence. |
| literature.quantity.populate | Read one literal specific activity or apparent Km from selected original JATS prose, or apparent Km from selected original HTML prose. Select quantity role and analyte, not numbers. HTML paragraphs without IDs use the explicit direct_paragraph:N selector within the selected section. Preserve untyped plus-minus spread. Subject-token presence does not establish experimental attribution; inspect the assay context separately. No comparison arms, conditions, product identity or missing correction score are invented. |
| literature.assay.populate | Interpret the source assay's actual subject, conditions, endpoint and molecular arrangement with exact source witnesses. Select reported numerical spans only when they have the stated correction-operand meanings. Deterministically parse and correct the interpreted source endpoint, preserving full covariance, conditional assumptions and unknowns. Exact quotes validate custody, not interpretation; no target transfer or annotation probability. |
| literature.ratio.populate | Read reported relative-signal percentages from selected JATS prose and optionally compare retained visual transcriptions with original image custody. Preserve the actual denominator/arrangement and conflicting candidate values. Signal is not calibrated molar amount or an isolated functional effect; no source reliability or target-transfer score is fabricated. |
| literature.binding.populate | Populate source binding-parameter components from an already received table or explicitly retained visual transcription. Keep IC50 distinct from reported Hill-fit Kd, actual protein/state/ligand identities, reported fit-spread basis and point/limit arithmetic. Original image custody is validated; no OCR, sampling confidence, intrinsic-affinity conversion or target credit is inferred. |
| literature.binding.model.populate | Evaluate the ordered parameter contrast in an actually received committed binding sheet using an explicitly supplied source model. Preserve full log-covariance measurement ownership, known versus estimated variance, and the stated threshold-reporting mechanism. Missing model source retains usable native contrast and explicit unknown likelihood cells. No inference of covariance from fit spreads or counts, limit-as-point calculation, intrinsic-affinity conversion, target transfer or annotation credit. |
| literature.transport.response.populate | Calculate a conditional source substrate-response correction from exact concentration spans and a received saved apparent-Km quantity. Preserve actual molecule, preparation, analyte, endpoint and fitted-curve contexts. Different or unknown curves leave the comparison unavailable. Full covariance retains physical owners and shared Km once; no sampling variance from untyped spread, target transfer or annotation credit is inferred. |
| literature.perturbation.populate | Populate reference perturbation/restoration components from source-bound design interpretations and optional received quantitative data. Keep actual recipient, changed component, partner, endpoint calibration and real restoration arms distinct. Qualitative-only outcomes cannot supply numerical rates. Preserve nuisance comparability separately from effect isolation and leave missing inputs/uncertainty unknown. No target transfer, necessity inference from an unmeasured catalytic knockout, or final annotation credit. |
| literature.structure.populate | Populate source-model geometry and local residue RSCC components from received coordinates and optional matching deposited validation. Select exact model/author atom groups and fixed physical criteria. Preserve missing endpoints, validation entry/revision mismatch and unreported coordinate uncertainty. The explicit scope is conditional deposited-model geometry; it does not establish population occupancy, causal mechanism, target correspondence or annotation credit. |
| literature.reaction.populate | Populate reported reference reaction-ratio residuals, named-prediction comparisons and simple resource-budget components from an explicitly retained received dataset or native source-selection recipe. Read exact report ratio points or author a:b expressions, summary uncertainty/counts and simple resource quantities with source units. Preserve unknown replication, missing alternatives, calibration basis and incomplete resource constraints. Product-pair ratios, instrument signals, supplied reagent budgets and usable capacity have distinct meanings. This route does not parse NMR spectra, establish measured oxygen coupling, apply missing corrections or calculate target transfer/annotation credit. |
| literature.context.populate | Populate biological context compatibility from source-bound retained observations and domain/route meanings. Keep organism capability distinct from fixed-sample coverage; preserve physical unit bases, missing local mapping, unexamined states, sample weights, pairing and conditional sampling design. Logical domain bounds are not confidence intervals or intuitive quality grades. Purified-enzyme assays are not automatically organism witnesses or habitat samples. No target correspondence or annotation credit is calculated. |
| literature.figure.populate | Read native experimental mean-bar ordinates from received original images using a retained linear-axis selection recipe. Preserve both subject/partner arms, endpoint and normalization meanings, source representation relationships, reported repeat/spread meanings and conditional digitization bounds. Return raw ordinates and a signed difference; pixel extraction does not supply SD, statistical significance, molar calibration, partner necessity or target credit. |
| literature.partner.populate | Populate source experimental partner-removal and addback components from received retained measurements and exact source witnesses. Preserve directed molecule/partner roles, nitrogen and other nonpartner conditions, normalization identity, physical measurement identity and reported spread meanings. Incompatible or incomplete comparisons keep native values and explicit unknown components. Censor domains are not confidence intervals; chemical bypass and partner swaps do not establish universal partner necessity, genomic presence, target transfer or annotation credit. |
| literature.partner.source.populate | Populate the same experimental partner components directly from selected literal source spans. Select complete rate/limit tokens, native units, spread meanings and source-bound entity/physical-measurement identities; do not supply scientific numbers or a prepared numeric JSON dataset. For source-defined activity units such as U/mg, select the endpoint-specific definition, quantity, molecular entity and time basis; no universal U conversion is assumed. Deterministic readers preserve original tokens, convert supported rate units and retain unknown normalization, conditions or observation identity. A repeated representation is not a new measurement. No sampling uncertainty, universal necessity, target correspondence or annotation credit is inferred. |
| literature.rate.source.populate | Populate the existing source-rate comparison sheet directly from selected literal paper spans, without a prepared CSV/TSV or model-authored scientific numbers. Request literature_rate_source_domain_cells for full reported-operand domains, including finite two-sided enclosures; the original literature_rate_source_cells projection preserves each arm's subject, construct, preparation, approximation and one-sided limits; literature_rate_cells is the separate legacy table projection. Select source-backed endpoint/basis relationships and statistical assumptions; different constructs may be the intended comparison. Source-defined U/mg requires its endpoint-specific definition. Missing meanings, unsupported units and censored values retain partial inputs. Exact witnesses verify custody, not causal isolation, target correspondence or annotation credit. |
| literature.amount.populate | Populate A105 source amount components from exact reported numerical/unit spans and witnessed experimental meanings. Keep target/total same-stock mass-fraction estimates separate from nominal molar amounts between arms. Preserve both quantity roles, preparations, methods, bases, bounds, approximation and source-owned covariance. Ratios above one and missing relationships remain explicit; no active fraction, universal activity correction, target transfer or annotation credit is inferred. The conditional mass-denominator factor is retained without applying it to a saved rate. |
| literature.optical.populate | Populate the existing net_rate and variance_net_rate input meanings from selected source-bound optical observations. Preserve NADH-depletion endpoint scope, actual subject/construct/preparation/conditions, qualified or missing inputs and source-owned covariance. Optical epsilon/path conversion is not recovery k, protein amount, product attribution or a complete activity score. Repeated representations create no independent evidence or annotation credit. |
| literature.kinetic.populate | Read source-bound reported Km, kcat or catalytic-efficiency estimates and populate native parameter, difference, ratio and log-contrast components for separately assayed substrates. Preserve actual molecule/construct, per-row protocols, qualifications and source uncertainty meanings. This native route has no covariance/model source reader; model-dependent evidence cells are not supported here, which is not a finding that the paper lacks covariance. No quotient of reported means, common-condition correction, intrinsic-affinity inference, target transfer or annotation credit. |
| literature.kinetic.model.populate | Populate the existing four conditional kinetic log-model cells from an actually received committed native kinetic sheet and an optional received retained model source. Model JSON uses a105_kinetic_log_model_v1 fields except source; provenance is bound from actual bytes. Preserve exact numerator/denominator physical estimate owners, natural-log canonical-parameter basis, full covariance, known/estimated/unknown variance and source interpretation witnesses. Reported SD/SEM/counts never supply covariance. These dependent parameter-contrast statistics are not assay reliability, function probabilities, target transfer or annotation credit. |
| literature.binding.interaction.populate | Read four selected original-image binding cells for two separately assayed source molecular forms and two ligands. Populate native IC50 or reported Hill-fit Kd parameters, within-form ligand ratios and their interaction/log interaction. Preserve actual source meanings, physical-fit identity, uncertain or conflicting readings, units, limits and partial uncertainty; unknown common kind retains raw results without choosing a default. Covariance/model source reading is unimplemented here, not a finding about the paper. No intrinsic-affinity conversion, target transfer or annotation credit. |
| knowledge.search | Search/page the run-frozen tool-instruction index. All whitespace-separated query terms must occur in entry metadata, case-insensitively; this is literal discovery, not a scientific suitability verdict. Empty query lists entries. No manual bodies are loaded. |
| knowledge.entry | Read one instruction entry's section index, tool names and provenance without loading manual bodies. A listed tool is not necessarily enabled for this episode. |
| knowledge.read | Read a selected instruction section by zero-based line offset and line count. Follow next_query for more. Returns run library identity and exact section digest; instructions are not scientific source evidence. |
| launch.instructions.search | Search/page the separate run-frozen launch instruction metadata. Empty query browses entries. resource_kind is an optional exact metadata filter; neither matches nor manuals establish resource availability. |
| launch.instructions.entry | Read one launch instruction entry index, sources and section hashes without loading section text. Listed operations still require an actual binding. |
| launch.instructions.read | Read exact zero-based line windows from a selected launch instruction section. Returns its digest and next_query; reading performs no setup or execution. |
| launch.instructions.select | Pin explicitly selected sections from one or multiple entries in this run-frozen launch library. Pass the returned selection as the child assignment launch_instructions. Does not choose or launch a resource. |
| episode.estimate_wait | Inspect the supported estimate for a proposed wait using your received progress, original duration snapshots and completed own-action history. Unknown event probabilities and gains remain unknown. This tool selects no wait, timer, resource or work. |
| episode.history | Read only this Episode's prior decisions: metadata index, exact selected actions/outcomes and admitted direct-child forms, or a bounded publication-ID page from one prior own action. Failed outcomes remain failed. This ordinary read never executes old work or reads child-private conversations. |
| episode.credit | Read the current credit projection for this Episode's fixed scope using this run's actual frozen projector and policy. The explicit limit and offset page source contributions and inactive dependencies independently; each includes its own total and next_offset. Zero limit requests metadata only. These are current source-bound operands, not biological accuracy or newly performed work. |
